purpose: Preserve the local micro-batch observations gathered in the ChatGPT project so future worker experiments can reuse the lessons without depending on this transcript.

source_runs.observed: One worker processed 5 heterogeneous local tasks (classification, extraction, writing, decomposition, audit) with no external tools and returned one bundle.

source_runs.observed_completion: 9/9 recovered outputs reported DONE with zero external reads/writes/tool_calls/retries and zero post-repair constraint failures.
source_runs.identity_anomaly: At least two different conversations emitted the same model-generated replica_id; model-authored replica ids are not execution authority.

candidate_lessons: Conceptual atomization does not require one chat or one durable write per atom; several independent atoms can be grouped inside one local micro-batch.
Prefer packet/context load once, local production of N useful atoms, local verification, then one result bundle/RETURN.
Model-authored timestamps and replica ids are descriptive only; external durable clocks and fresh beacon/claim identity remain authoritative.
Explicit zero-I/O fields may reinforce instruction retention but are not a security mechanism; absence/restriction of tools and external verification are stronger.
Increase local batch size until quality, instruction retention, completeness or verification degrades; speed alone never selects a winner.
Measure number of decisions and amount of generated output separately; a worker may tolerate many classifications but fewer long-form outputs.
Do not infer the same result for material/tool-using tasks until separately tested.
experiment_boundary: These observations came from project-chat experiments rather than a runner-controlled benchmark. They justify a bounded E5 local-batch experiment, not a baseline protocol change.
